title: People
goal: Say what someone is like — personality, looks, who they're related to — talk about friends, partners and family politics, pass on a bit of gossip, and use full relative clauses and 'seems / looks like'.
intro:
Half of all conversation is about other people: the new colleague, a cousin's fiancé, the friend who never pays, the aunt everyone is a little afraid of. This unit gives you the adjectives for **personality** (ملنسار، ضدي، ڪنجوس، ڪاهل…) and **looks**, the words for the people in a Sindhi family's orbit (ڪزن، ڀاڄائي، سس، منگيتر), and the language of **gossip** — گپ شپ.

Grammar: **relative clauses in full** — **جنهن** سان شادي ٿي رهي آهي 'the one he's marrying', **جنهن جو** ڀاءُ 'whose brother', and the handy short cut **ڪراچيءَ وارو** ڪزن 'the cousin from Karachi' — plus **لڳڻ** for 'seems / looks (like)'.

grammar.title: Relative clauses in full: جنهن، جن، and the وارو short cut
grammar.body:
In Unit 20 you met the two-part relative sentence: **جيڪو** ماڻهو ڪالهه آيو هو، **سو** منهنجو چاچو آهي. Here is the full system.

**1. The j-word agrees** with the person or thing: **جيڪو** (m sg) · **جيڪا** (f sg) · **جيڪي** (pl). The pointer in the second half matches it: **سو / سا / سي**, or in everyday speech **اهو / اها / اهي**.

**2. Before any postposition** the j-word is oblique: **جنهن** janhin (sg) · **جن** jin (pl) — and the pointer goes oblique too: **ان** un / **انهن** unhan.

**جنهن جو** ڀاءُ — whose brother (جو agrees with what is owned: جنهن **جي** ڀيڻ، جنهن **جا** ٻار)
**جنهن سان** شادي ٿي رهي آهي — the one (he's) marrying
**جنهن کي** مون پئسا ڏنا — the one I gave money to
**جن** ڪزنن سان کيڏندو هوس — the cousins I used to play with

**3. In the ergative past** the j-word is oblique as the doer: **جنهن** مون کي ٻڌايو، **ان** کان پڇو 'ask the person who told me'.

**4. Whoever / whatever**: add **به**: **جيڪو به** اچي 'whoever comes', **جنهن کي به** پڇو 'whoever you ask'.

**5. 'So … that'**: **اهڙو** (اهڙي، اهڙا) … **جو** …: هو **اهڙو** ضدي آهي **جو** ڪنهن جي نٿو ٻڌي 'he's so stubborn (that) he won't listen to anyone'.

**6. The short cut: وارو.** Instead of a whole clause, Sindhi often uses **oblique infinitive + وارو** or **noun + وارو** (agreeing: واري، وارا):
مٿي **رهڻ وارو** ڇوڪرو — the boy who lives upstairs
**چشمي واري** ڇوڪري — the girl with glasses
**ڪراچيءَ وارو** ڪزن — the cousin from Karachi

**Trap:** never use the question word ڪنهن for a relative: 'the man whose car…' is **جنهن** جي گاڏي, not ڪنهن جي گاڏي (that means 'someone's car' / 'whose car?').

grammar.title: Seems, looks, comes across: لڳڻ
grammar.body:
To describe how someone **seems** or **looks**, Sindhi uses **لڳڻ** laɠaṇu 'to strike, seem' (you met it with weather and with لڳي ٿو ته… in Unit 13).

**1. Person + adjective + لڳي ٿو** — the verb agrees with the person:
هو ٿڪل **لڳي ٿو** — he looks tired · هوءَ خوش **لڳي ٿي** — she looks happy
اهي پريشان **لڳن ٿا** — they look worried · تون **لڳين ٿو / ٿي** — you look (intimate) · توهان **لڳو ٿا** — you look (polite) · مان **لڳان ٿو** — I look

**2. 'Struck me as' — مون کي + person + adjective + لڳو / لڳي** (past = a first impression):
مون کي هو مغرور **لڳو** — he struck me as arrogant · مون کي هوءَ سٺي **لڳي** — I thought she was nice

**3. Looks like someone — … جهڙو لڳڻ**, with جهڙو agreeing with the person described:
تون پيءُ **جهڙو** لڳين ٿو · هوءَ ماءُ **جهڙي** لڳي ٿي · ٻئي ڀائر هڪ ٻئي **جهڙا** لڳن ٿا

**4. Appearance vs reality — ڏسڻ ۾ ته … پر …** 'to look at … but …': ڏسڻ ۾ ته سادو لڳي ٿو، پر ڏاڍو هوشيار آهي. The little **ته** marks the contrast that's coming.

**5. Guessing — لڳي ٿو ته …** 'it seems that …': لڳي ٿو ته هنن جو جهيڙو ٿيو آهي.

Note that **پسند اچڻ** or **وڻڻ** say whether you *like* someone; لڳڻ says how they *come across*. 'I like him' = هو مون کي وڻي ٿو.

culture:
**Family is the main topic.** In Sindh people place you by your family first — 'whose son are you?', 'which village are your people from?' — and a huge share of everyday talk is about cousins, in-laws and who is marrying whom. Matches (**رشتا**) are still mostly arranged or 'arranged-love': families meet, there's a **منگڻي** (engagement), and the whole extended family has an opinion. Many marriages are within the extended family, so a cousin can also be a fiancé.

**Describing people**: Sindhis praise character more than looks — **نيڪ**, **ملنسار**, **سخي** are high compliments, and calling someone **ڪنجوس** or **مغرور** is a real criticism. Be careful with comments on weight and skin colour: they're common in the older generation but many younger people find them rude. **سمارٽ** is a safe compliment.

**Gossip** (**گپ شپ**) is a social glue — over chai, at weddings, on the phone with cousins — and it usually starts with **ڪنهن کي نه ٻڌائجو، پر…**, which everyone knows means the opposite. The polite way out of gossip you don't want to join is a laugh and **ڇڏ يار** or **الله ڄاڻي** 'God knows'. Among friends, teasing (**مذاق**) is affectionate: **چريو** 'crazy' is often a term of endearment.

tip.title: Adjectives: which ones change?
tip.body:
- -o adjectives agree: **شرميلو** (m) · **شرميلي** (f) · **شرميلا** (pl).
- Most borrowed ones never change: ملنسار، سخي، نيڪ، ڪنجوس.
- ڏاڍو 'very' agrees too: **ڏاڍي** ملنسار (f).
- 'What kind of…?' = **ڪهڙي قسم جو / جي** + person.

tip.title: Seems, looks: لڳڻ
tip.body:
- Person + adjective + **لڳي ٿو / ٿي**: هو ٿڪل **لڳي ٿو**، هوءَ خوش **لڳي ٿي**. You: **لڳين ٿو** (intimate), **لڳو ٿا** (polite).
- First impression: **مون کي** هو مغرور **لڳو**.
- **ڏسڻ ۾ ته** … لڳي ٿو، **پر** … = looks … but actually …

lessons.title: Describing looks

tip.title: Looks like someone: … جهڙو لڳڻ
tip.body:
- **جهڙو** agrees with the person described: هو پيءُ **جهڙو** لڳي ٿو، هوءَ ماءُ **جهڙي** لڳي ٿي، اهي **جهڙا** لڳن ٿا.
- Looks with آهي: هن جو **قد** ڊگهو آهي، هوءَ **چشمو** پائي ٿي.
- **سمارٽ** = slim, well-turned-out — not 'clever'.

new: تون پنهنجي پيءُ جهڙو لڳين ٿو.

sentences.native: تنهنجي ڀيڻ بلڪل تو جهڙي لڳي ٿي.
sentences.roman: tunhinjī bheṇa bilkul to jhaṛī laɠe thī.
sentences.en: Your sister looks just like you.

sentences.native: ٻئي ڀائر هڪ ٻئي جهڙا لڳن ٿا.
sentences.roman: ɓaī bhāura hika ɓie jhaṛā laɠan thā.
sentences.en: The two brothers look alike.

sentences.native: هن جو قد ڊگهو آهي.
sentences.roman: hun jo qadu ḍigho āhe.
sentences.en: He's tall.

sentences.native: هن جو قد ننڍو آهي، پر ڏاڍو سمارٽ آهي.
sentences.roman: hun jo qadu nanḍho āhe, para ɗāḍho smārṭu āhe.
sentences.en: He's short, but he looks really sharp.

sentences.native: چشمي ۾ تون پنهنجي استاد جهڙو لڳين ٿو!
sentences.roman: chashme meṃ tūṃ panhinje ustāda jhaṛo laɠeṃ tho!
sentences.en: With glasses on you look like your teacher!

sentences.native: هوءَ چشمو پائي ٿي.
sentences.roman: hūa chashmo pāe thī.
sentences.en: She wears glasses.

sentences.native: شڪل مان ته ڪراچيءَ جو لڳي ٿو.
sentences.roman: shakila māṃ ta karāchīa jo laɠe tho.
sentences.en: By the look of him, he's from Karachi.

sentences.native: هن جي شڪل پنهنجي ڏاڏي جهڙي آهي.
sentences.roman: hun jī shakila panhinje ɗāɗe jhaṛī āhe.
sentences.en: He's got his grandfather's face.

sentences.native: اڄڪلهه تون ڏاڍي سمارٽ لڳين ٿي!
sentences.roman: aʄkalha tūṃ ɗāḍhī smārṭu laɠīṃ thī!
sentences.en: You're looking really slim these days! (to a woman, informal)

lessons.title: Friends, fiancés and in-laws

tip.title: The one who… — جنهن، جن
tip.body:
- **جيڪو / جيڪا / جيڪي** agree with the person; point back with **اهو / اها / اهي** (or سو / سا / سي).
- Before کي، سان، جو… use **جنهن** (sg) / **جن** (pl): **جنهن سان** شادي ٿي رهي آهي، **جنهن جو** رشتو آيو.
- Never ڪنهن here — that's the question word.

new: هيءَ منهنجي سڀ کان پراڻي سهيلي آهي.
ان جو رشتو پڪو ٿي ويو آهي.
هو ڪنهن سان شادي ڪري رهيو آهي؟

sentences.native: جنهن ڇوڪريءَ سان هو شادي ڪري رهيو آهي، اها منهنجي سهيلي آهي.
sentences.roman: janhin chhokirīa sāṃ hū shādī kare rahyo āhe, uhā munhinjī sahelī āhe.
sentences.en: The girl he's marrying is my friend.

sentences.native: جنهن ڪزن جي شادي آهي، سا ڪراچيءَ ۾ رهي ٿي.
sentences.roman: janhin kazin jī shādī āhe, sā karāchīa meṃ rahe thī.
sentences.en: The cousin who's getting married lives in Karachi.

sentences.native: جيڪي ماڻهو منگڻيءَ تي آيا هئا، سي سڀ هن جا ڪزن هئا.
sentences.roman: jeke māṇhū manganīa te āyā huā, se sabhu hun jā kazin huā.
sentences.en: The people who came to the engagement were all his cousins.

sentences.native: جنهن جو رشتو آيو آهي، اهو ڇوڪرو ڇا ٿو ڪري؟
sentences.roman: janhin jo rishto āyo āhe, uho chhokiro chhā tho kare?
sentences.en: The boy who's sent the proposal — what does he do?

sentences.native: جن ڪزنن سان مان کيڏندو هوس، اهي هاڻي ٻاهر رهن ٿا.
sentences.roman: jin kazinan sāṃ māṃ kheɗando hos, uhe hāṇe ɓāhari rahan thā.
sentences.en: The cousins I used to play with live abroad now.

sentences.native: منهنجي سس ڏاڍي سٺي آهي، پر ٿوري ضدي آهي.
sentences.roman: munhinjī sasu ɗāḍhī suṭhī āhe, para thorī zidī āhe.
sentences.en: My mother-in-law is really nice, but a bit stubborn.

sentences.native: منهنجي ڀاڄائي ڪراچيءَ جي آهي.
sentences.roman: munhinjī bhāʄāī karāchīa jī āhe.
sentences.en: My sister-in-law is from Karachi.

sentences.native: هن جو منگيتر ٻاهر ڪم ڪري ٿو.
sentences.roman: hun jo mangetara ɓāhari kamu kare tho.
sentences.en: Her fiancé works abroad.

sentences.native: توهان جي سهيليءَ جو نالو ڇا آهي؟
sentences.roman: tavhāṃ jī sahelīa jo nālo chhā āhe?
sentences.en: What's your friend's name?

lessons.title: Who's who, and who's not speaking to whom

tip.title: Short cuts: وارو, and اهڙو … جو
tip.body:
- **وارو** (واري، وارا) replaces a whole clause: مٿي **رهڻ وارو** ڇوڪرو 'the boy who lives upstairs', **چشمي واري** ڇوڪري 'the girl with glasses'.
- **اهڙو … جو** = so … that: **اهڙو** ضدي آهي **جو** ڪنهن جي نٿو ٻڌي.
- Both agree with the person.

sentences.native: ڪراچيءَ وارو ڪزن سڀاڻي ايندو.
sentences.roman: karāchīa vāro kazin subhāṇe endo.
sentences.en: My cousin from Karachi is coming tomorrow.

sentences.native: ڊگهن وارن واري ڇوڪري هن جي منگيتر آهي.
sentences.roman: ḍighan vāran vārī chhokirī hun jī mangetara āhe.
sentences.en: The girl with long hair is his fiancée.

sentences.native: مٿي رهڻ وارا پاڙيسري ڏاڍا ملنسار آهن.
sentences.roman: mathe rahaṇa vārā pāṛesirī ɗāḍhā milansāru āhin.
sentences.en: The neighbours who live upstairs are really friendly.

sentences.native: هو اهڙو ضدي آهي جو ڪنهن جي ڳالهه ئي نٿو ٻڌي.
sentences.roman: hū ahiṛo zidī āhe jo kanhin jī ɠālhi ī natho ɓudhe.
sentences.en: He's so stubborn he won't listen to anyone.

sentences.native: اهي ٻئي پاڻ ۾ اهڙا دوست آهن جو هر روز ملن ٿا.
sentences.roman: uhe ɓaī pāṇa meṃ ahiṛā dosta āhin jo har roz milan thā.
sentences.en: Those two are such good friends they meet every day.

sentences.native: ڀائرن ۾ وري جهيڙو ٿيو.
sentences.roman: bhāuran meṃ varī jhero thiyo.
sentences.en: The brothers had another fight.

sentences.native: ننڍي ڳالهه تي جهيڙو نه ڪريو.
sentences.roman: nanḍhī ɠālhi te jhero na karyo.
sentences.en: Don't fight over a little thing.

sentences.native: امان ۽ ڀاڄائي جي پاڻ ۾ سٺي ٺهي ٿي.
sentences.roman: amāṃ ai bhāʄāī jī pāṇa meṃ suṭhī ṭhahe thī.
sentences.en: Mum and my sister-in-law get on well.

sentences.native: جنهن ڏينهن کان جهيڙو ٿيو آهي، اهي پاڻ ۾ نٿا ڳالهائين.
sentences.roman: janhin ɗīṃha khāṃ jhero thiyo āhe, uhe pāṇa meṃ nathā ɠālhāin.
sentences.en: Since the day they fought, they haven't been speaking to each other.

lessons.title: A bit of gossip

tip.title: Gossip lines
tip.body:
- Open: **ڪنهن کي نه ٻڌائجو، پر…** (everyone knows what that means).
- React: **سچي؟** · **ڇا ٿو چوين!** 'you don't say!'
- Get out of it: **ڇڏ يار، ان جي ڳالهه نه ڪر.**
- **گپ شپ** is harmless chat; talking behind someone's back is **پويان ڳالهائڻ**.

new: ڇڏ يار، ان جي ڳالهه نه ڪر.

sentences.native: اچو ته ٿوري گپ شپ ڪريون.
sentences.roman: acho ta thorī gapa shapa karyūṃ.
sentences.en: Let's have a bit of a chat.

sentences.native: ڪنهن کي نه ٻڌائجو، پر هن جو رشتو ٽٽي ويو.
sentences.roman: kanhin khe na ɓudhāijo, para hun jo rishto ṭuṭī vayo.
sentences.en: Don't tell anyone, but her engagement's been called off.

sentences.native: مان ته رڳو مذاق پيو ڪريان!
sentences.roman: māṃ ta raɠo mazāqu peyo karyāṃ!
sentences.en: I'm only joking! (man)

sentences.native: هو هر ڳالهه کي مذاق ۾ وٺي ٿو.
sentences.roman: hū har ɠālhi khe mazāqa meṃ vaṭhe tho.
sentences.en: He takes everything as a joke.

sentences.native: ماڻهن جي پويان ڳالهائڻ سٺي ڳالهه ناهي.
sentences.roman: māṇhan je poyāṃ ɠālhāiṇu suṭhī ɠālhi nāhe.
sentences.en: Talking behind people's backs isn't nice.

sentences.native: ڇا ٿو چوين! هن کي نوڪري ملي وئي؟
sentences.roman: chhā tho chaveṃ! hun khe nokirī milī vaī?
sentences.en: You don't say! He got a job?

sentences.native: هي سڄو قصو توکي ڪنهن ٻڌايو؟
sentences.roman: hī saʄo qiso tokhe kanhin ɓudhāyo?
sentences.en: Who told you this whole story?

sentences.native: اسين سڄي رات گپ شپ ڪندا رهياسين.
sentences.roman: asīṃ saʄī rāti gapa shapa kandā rahyāsīṃ.
sentences.en: We chatted all night.

sentences.native: هن سان مذاق نه ڪر، هوءَ جلدي ناراض ٿي ويندي آهي.
sentences.roman: hun sāṃ mazāqu na karu, hūa jaldī nārāzu thī vendī āhe.
sentences.en: Don't joke around with her — she gets upset easily. (informal)
